title: Tenant scheduler label remap left pods orphaned during on-prem operator upgrade; rescue + hotfix
creator: Sofia Chen
description: During a staged on-prem operator upgrade we observed tenant pods being assigned new node labels that our scheduler does not recognize. The result: existing workloads entered a 'Pending' or 'Unknown' state (zombie pods) for affected tenants; customers reported degraded service and stuck inference pipelines. This ticket coordinates triage, a tactical hotfix to restore scheduling affinity, and a follow-on fix to avoid label remapping in future upgrades.
steps_to_reproduce: Run operator v3.9.0 -> v3.9.1 staged upgrade in lab tenant with node-label-sync enabled
Observe node labels applied by the operator post-upgrade (e.g., redwood.io/tenant-shard -> redwood.io/tenant-shard:v2)
Deploy a long-running pod with nodeSelector redwood.io/tenant-shard:legacy and confirm it becomes Pending after upgrade
Check operator controller logs for label sync events and kubelet events for scheduling failures
observed_behavior: Pods that were previously scheduled became Pending and never bound
Controller reported 'label/mask' updates in operator logs around upgrade time
KV cache sees tenant node label keys with duplicated suffixes (legacy vs v2) leading to scheduler mismatch
Affected tenants reported 50-200ms API latencies and worker restarts
impact_summary: Three customers (alpha, beta, gamma) experienced failing on-prem inference pods during staged upgrades. Immediate customer impact included request timeouts and degraded throughput on Dedicated/private workloads. Estimated customer downtime window ranged from 12 minutes to 2 hours depending on tenant size and manual remediation.
mitigation_steps_taken: Added emergency reconciler to operator to detect duplicate label variants and create alias entries for scheduler
Rolled forward a reversible configmap that forces label aliasing for affected tenants
Open PR to add a pre-upgrade validation hook to detect label schema changes and block upgrade if mismatched
Communicated mitigations and temporary workarounds to the SRE/customer success teams
temporary_workarounds: kubectl patch node to add legacy label key for nodes in affected clusters
Restart operator with --label-aliasing=true to enable compatibility mapping
Manual eviction and reschedule of Pending pods after label patch
root_cause: A change in the operator's node label canonicalization introduced a new suffix pattern (':v2') for tenancy shard labels. The internal scheduler matcher only recognized legacy keys. During staged upgrades the operator reapplied labels, creating both legacy and v2 variants in different timing windows. The scheduler lookup is strict and failed to match the new keys, leaving pods unschedulable.
proposed_long_term_fix: Introduce a label compatibility layer in the operator that maintains stable canonical keys across upgrades
Update scheduler matcher to accept alias patterns and fall back to legacy keys for 30 days post-upgrade
Add an operator preflight check that computes diff between before/after label sets and warns/blocks upgrade if non-backwards-compatible
Add e2e upgrade tests covering label canonicalization and scheduler integration
acceptance_criteria: Operator release contains label-compat shim and scheduler accepts alias patterns
Upgrade tests validate no tenant pod remains Pending in staging during rolling upgrades
Customers from the pilot cohort (alpha/beta) report no recurrence on their next scheduled upgrade
Runbook updated and SRE runbook verified in a chaos test
